title: Trace delegate invocation and captured state, including lifetime and multicast failure behavior

rubric.point: Both delegates from one call capture the same variable storage, rather than separate copies of its initial value.
The two Advance calls change that shared count from 6 to 9 to 12, which Read observes.
The reachable returned delegates retain the captured state, allowing it to outlive the method call.
A second CreateCounter call creates a separate captured count initialized to 6.

questions.model:
Both lambdas capture the same `count` variable, not snapshots of `6`. Each `Advance()` changes that shared storage, first to `9` and then to `12`, so `Read()` returns `12`.

The returned delegates keep the captured state reachable after `CreateCounter` returns. Returning from the method therefore does not end that state's lifetime. A second call creates its own captured variable initialized to `6`; its delegates do not share the first counter's state.

rubric.point: Handlers run synchronously in registration order; the second handler throws and the third is skipped.
The first handler's increment remains, giving completed == 1; the exception does not roll back that change.
batch() never returns normally, so assignment to result does not occur and the earlier return value 20 is not used.
The outer catch receives control after multicast invocation has unwound; attempting later handlers requires enumerating GetInvocationList() and catching failures separately around each handler call.

questions.model:
The first handler runs, increments `completed` to `1`, and returns `20`. The second handler then throws. Invocation stops, so the third handler never adds `10`. The first increment is not rolled back.

Because `batch()` throws instead of returning normally, `result = batch()` never performs its assignment. `result` stays `-1`; the earlier handler's `20` is not a fallback result.

The outer catch handles the exception after control has left the multicast invocation. It does not resume the invocation list. To attempt later handlers despite failures, enumerate `batch.GetInvocationList()` and invoke each entry inside its own `try/catch`.
